simple.meaning: נְחָשׁ (nᵉchâsh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “copper.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 2:32. The surrounding context includes kingship, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְחָשׁ (H5174) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: נְחָשׁ (nᵉchâsh) / H5174 is traced through Daniel 2:32, Daniel 2:35, Daniel 2:39, Daniel 2:45 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: As for this image, its head was of fine gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,

timeline.evidenceText: As for this image, its head was of fine gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,

Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were broken in pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors. The wind carried them away, so that no place was found for them. The stone that struck the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
“After you, another kingdom will arise that is inferior to you; and another third kingdom of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.

Because you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God has made known to the king what will happen hereafter. The dream is certain, and its interpretation sure.”

The leaves of it were beautiful, and it had much fruit, and in it was food for all. The animals of the field had shade under it, and the birds of the sky lived in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.
The tree that you saw, which grew, and was strong, whose height reached to the sky, and its sight to all the earth;
They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of bronze, of iron, of wood, and of stone.

but have lifted up yourself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before you, and you and your lords, your wives, and your concubines, have drunk wine from them. You have praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which don’t see, or hear, or know; and you have not glorified the God in whose hand your breath is, and whose are all your ways.

“Then I desired to know the truth concerning the fourth animal, which was different from all of them, exceedingly terrible, whose teeth were of iron, and its nails of bronze; which devoured, broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet;

definitions.full: H5174. nechash נְחָשׁ noun masculine copper, bronze ( ᵑ7 Syriac; Biblical Hebrew נְחוּשָׁה נְחשֶׁת, , √ III. נחשׁ ); — as material: absolute ׳נ Dan 2:32 ; 4:12 ; 4:20 ; 7:19 ; emphatic נְחָשָׁא 2:35 , 39 , 45 ; 5:4 , 23 .
